text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The United States rejects a U.N. resolution requiring Israel to pay more than $1.7 million for damage resulting from its shelling of a U.N. base at Qana in south Lebanon last year.
- Five Red Army guerrillas on trial in Beirut.
- Lebanon's budget deficit at 56.3 percent in May.
- World Bank president makes implicit criticism during Beirut visit.
- Foreign Minister Bouez: Waiting for U.S. explanations on reports that the administration threatened to withdraw U.N. peacekeeping troops from south Lebanon.
- Japanese Red Army denied charges and said they were arrested for political reasons.
- Nominal surplus of treasury bill subscription against maturity down to 67 billion pounds.
- The five-nation group monitoring ceasefire in Lebanon holds Israel responsible for roadside bomb outside south Lebanon occupation zone after 21-hour meeting.
- Bank of Beirut rises again in Beirut.
- An Iraqi commercial delegation to visit Beirut next month according to Iraqi newspaper.
